title: Shallow-history fitness gain under independent assay blocks

source.claim_location: Methods: competition assays; Results: shallow-history analysis
source.evidence_statement: The primary study reports negative initial-fitness versus fitness-change correlations in 15 of 16 comparisons and uses fourfold fitness-assay replication.

system.phenomenon: Fitness change in experimentally evolved E. coli populations
system.scope_boundary: Controlled environments and the shallow-history comparisons in the cited experiment.

design.unit_description: Evolutionary population measured within a fitness assay block
design.exposure_or_comparator: Ancestral fitness compared with subsequent fitness change
design.time_structure: Baseline and later assay measurements across four blocks

measurement.measurement_rule: Competition assays estimate ancestral fitness and later fitness change with reported uncertainty.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: Assay error enters both the baseline and the derived change score.

inference.published_claim: Fitter ancestral populations tend to gain less fitness.
inference.scope_boundary: The reported association is not a universal biological mechanism.

validation.published_baseline: Published-style correlation of initial fitness with fitness change.
validation.independent_check: Cross-fit baseline and change from disjoint assay blocks.

fragility.mechanism: A noisy baseline is reused with opposite sign inside the change score.
fragility.alternative_explanation: Mathematical coupling can create or exaggerate a negative correlation.
fragility.decisive_test: Estimate baseline and change from independent assay blocks before fitting the association.

provenance.data_location: Official archive manifest and verified raw files

decision.plain_language: The striking pattern became much weaker when the starting measurement and later change were separated.
limitations: The independent-block estimate is attenuated and uncertain, not a definitive biological refutation.
Assay-block exchangeability and one planned sensitivity remain open.

title: Repeated animals, infection status, and seasonal fat change

source.claim_location: Methods: energetic-cost GLMMs; Discussion and Conclusions
source.evidence_statement: The study models seasonal fat change with animal ID as a random intercept and interprets pathogen-associated reductions as energetic costs.

system.phenomenon: Seasonal fat change and pathogen status in bighorn sheep
system.scope_boundary: Repeated animal-season intervals from the study herds.

design.unit_description: Animal-season interval with repeated animal identifiers
design.exposure_or_comparator: Current pathogen status and acquisition or clearance status
design.time_structure: Repeated observations across seasons and herds

measurement.measurement_rule: The file records current and prior fat, pathogen variables, and covariates for each interval.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: Single-capture pathogen detection and unmeasured behavioral covariates remain imperfect.

inference.published_claim: Pathogen status has an energetic cost expressed as fat loss.
inference.scope_boundary: The observational association does not identify a causal mechanism.

validation.published_baseline: Mixed model with animal ID random intercept.
validation.independent_check: Separate within-animal exposure changes from stable between-animal differences and leave out herds.

fragility.mechanism: A random intercept does not distinguish within-animal variation from stable animal or herd differences.
fragility.alternative_explanation: Food, contact behavior, habitat, or immune state can jointly affect infection and fat.
fragility.decisive_test: Compare within-between and individual-fixed-effect sensitivity models across predeclared partitions.

decision.plain_language: The data can test whether the association follows the same animal, but cannot by itself prove why it does.
limitations: Residual time-varying confounding prevents causal interpretation.
Domain and longitudinal-inference specialist review remains required.

title: Source-extraction decisions in a shared meta-analysis database

source.evidence_statement: The database retains constituent-database identity and potential duplicates and flags contrasting conclusions and data-extractor bias as an analysis opportunity.

system.phenomenon: Global-change experimental findings combined across multiple evidence databases
system.scope_boundary: Extracted records and pooled moderator conclusions in the frozen MESI archive.

design.unit_description: Extracted outcome record linked to experiment and constituent database
design.exposure_or_comparator: Treatment versus control summaries and alternative extraction decisions
design.time_structure: Cross-sectional evidence synthesis of prior experiments

measurement.measurement_rule: Records contain treatment/control summaries, uncertainty, replication, units, and metadata.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: Duplicate and aggregation labels do not guarantee estimand equivalence.

inference.published_claim: Pooled moderator conclusions describe global-change responses.
inference.scope_boundary: The cell concerns reproducibility of the evidence table, not a new ecological mechanism.

validation.published_baseline: Published pooled analyses of the constituent evidence records.
validation.independent_check: Predeclare record matching, duplicate handling, and extraction reconciliation before recomputing selected effects.

fragility.mechanism: Extraction, duplicate handling, and aggregation determine which records enter a pooled estimate.
fragility.alternative_explanation: Apparent disagreement can reflect non-equivalent outcomes rather than researcher error.
fragility.decisive_test: Audit matched source records under a frozen reconciliation protocol.

decision.plain_language: A conclusion can change because the evidence table was built differently, not because the experiments changed.
limitations: A current conference result narrows novelty for this reconciliation question.
Author-overlap and specialist review remain unresolved.

title: Aging shifts the calibration curve used for voltage diagnosis

source.evidence_statement: The paper reports that using a fresh-cell open-circuit-voltage curve degrades aged-cell accuracy and identifies joint curve estimation as a needed extension.

system.phenomenon: Voltage-based diagnosis of lithium-ion cells across aging conditions
system.scope_boundary: The cells, conditions, and diagnostic setting represented in the cited archive.

design.unit_description: Cell trajectory under a documented operating condition
design.exposure_or_comparator: Fresh versus aged condition-specific OCV curve

measurement.measurement_rule: Voltage, current, temperature, capacity, resistance, and OCV curves are recorded for experimental cells.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: The reference curve may change with condition rather than represent a fixed instrument calibration.

inference.published_claim: Voltage-controlled diagnosis can identify capacity and resistance.
inference.scope_boundary: Prediction depends on the compatibility of the OCV reference curve and cell condition.

validation.published_baseline: Diagnostic evaluation using known condition-specific curves.
validation.independent_check: Evaluate a reference curve learned in one condition on an aged-cell condition.

fragility.mechanism: The calibration curve changes with the physical state being diagnosed.
fragility.alternative_explanation: Apparent prediction failure can be reference mismatch rather than parameter non-identifiability.
fragility.decisive_test: Compare fresh-curve and condition-specific-curve performance on separately evaluated cells.

provenance.data_location: Experimental CSV files, condition-specific OCV curves, and MATLAB inventory

decision.plain_language: A diagnostic method can look accurate until the reference curve changes with the thing being diagnosed.
limitations: The closest paper already demonstrates this boundary and names the needed extension.
A new target needs a distinct scientific consequence.

title: Model-triggered biocontrol evaluated from epidemic summaries

source.evidence_statement: The study compares calendar and model strategies across four epidemics and reports an epidemic-by-treatment analysis.

system.scope_boundary: Four reported epidemics and the published treatment strategies.

design.unit_description: Treatment-by-epidemic summary rather than individual plot outcome

measurement.measurement_rule: The deposited file reports disease-severity means and standard errors by treatment and epidemic.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: Plot-level outcomes and application events are absent from the public table.

inference.published_claim: A model-triggered strategy can retain efficacy while reducing applications.
inference.scope_boundary: The existing study already reports epidemic-by-treatment analysis.

validation.published_baseline: Published treatment comparison across four epidemics.
validation.independent_check: No public plot-level partition or event record is available for the proposed robustness test.

fragility.mechanism: Aggregate summaries discard units and timing needed for independent robustness analysis.
fragility.alternative_explanation: An apparent across-epidemic result may depend on unobserved plot-level variation or applications.
fragility.decisive_test: Acquire plot-level outcomes and application events, then hold out epidemics or plots.

decision.plain_language: The question may be important, but the public table is too compressed to test it properly.
limitations: The closest paper already tested the proposed interaction.

title: Early magnetic signal proposed as a fatigue-life predictor

source.evidence_statement: The paper fits an M–N relationship and reports early-life correlations using the same 19 soft-magnetic-iron specimens.

system.phenomenon: Fatigue life prediction from early magnetic measurements
system.scope_boundary: Soft-magnetic-iron specimens and the five materials described by the archive.

design.unit_description: Physical specimen with force, displacement, and magnetic measurements
design.exposure_or_comparator: Early magnetic drift compared with later fatigue life
design.time_structure: Early-life signal and later specimen failure

measurement.measurement_rule: The official metadata describes time, force, displacement, and magnetic-field data by specimen.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: The real files could not be acquired to verify variables or specimen identifiers.

inference.published_claim: Early magnetic drift predicts fatigue life.
inference.scope_boundary: The claim requires evaluation beyond the specimens used to fit the reported relation.

validation.published_baseline: Reported early-life correlations and fitted M–N relation.
validation.independent_check: Specimen-held-out and leave-one-material-out validation cannot be run without files.

fragility.mechanism: No real-sample audit is possible while the public archive is inaccessible.
fragility.alternative_explanation: The apparent predictor may be driven by reuse of specimens for fitting and evaluation.
fragility.decisive_test: Acquire official files and evaluate held-out specimens and materials.

provenance.data_location: Official file metadata and failed content retrieval receipt

decision.plain_language: A persuasive validation question cannot be checked until the actual public files can be acquired.
limitations: Official retrieval returned HTTP 403 during the documented attempts.
Landing-page metadata cannot establish variable adequacy.

title: Correlated responses across evolution and assay environments

source.evidence_statement: The archive reports cross-environment correlated responses and provides population, evolution environment, assay environment, ancestral growth rate, and absolute and relative growth-rate change.

system.phenomenon: Experimental evolution of Tetrahymena across environmental conditions
system.scope_boundary: The population, evolution-environment, and assay-environment combinations in the archive.

design.unit_description: Population measured under evolution and assay environments
design.exposure_or_comparator: Evolution environment and assay environment combinations
design.outcome: Growth rate and change relative to ancestral growth
design.time_structure: Ancestral and post-evolution measurements across conditions

measurement.measurement_rule: Growth curves from a microplate reader are summarized by growth-rate, ancestor, and change columns.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: Technical replication and whether derived changes reuse the same measured baseline remain unverified.

inference.published_claim: Diminishing returns can hold across environments and correlated responses can be asymmetric.
inference.scope_boundary: The record supports a future robustness question, not a claim of universal evolutionary dynamics.

validation.published_baseline: Reported growth-rate patterns across evolution and assay conditions.
validation.independent_check: Audit raw assay structure and, if available, separate baseline estimation from derived change.

fragility.mechanism: An ancestral growth measure may be reused inside relative or absolute change calculations.
fragility.alternative_explanation: A derived-score relationship can reflect mathematical coupling rather than cross-environment biology.
fragility.decisive_test: Verify the raw assay layout and estimate the relationship from independent measurements if possible.

provenance.data_location: Dryad file inventory and README, lines 25–62

decision.plain_language: This is a possible independent test of a familiar pattern, not yet a new target.
limitations: Raw rows and file checksums have not been inspected.
Prior-art and specialist review have not been run.

title: Icing and summer warming effects measured repeatedly at tundra plots

source.evidence_statement: The archive describes a five-winter full-factorial field experiment with plot-level soil, vegetation, biomass, flower, and phenology measurements.

system.phenomenon: Tundra plant response to experimental icing and summer warming
system.scope_boundary: The experiment's plots, winters, and measured plant-response outcomes.

design.unit_description: Experimental plot followed across treatments and years
design.exposure_or_comparator: Rain-on-snow icing and increased summer temperature treatments
design.outcome: Phenology, productivity, reproduction, and environmental measurements
design.time_structure: Five consecutive winters with repeated plot-level observations

measurement.measurement_rule: The archive reports plot-level environmental, biomass, flower-count, leaf-trait, and phenology measurements.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: The raw plot IDs, missingness, and outcome-selection rules have not yet been audited.

inference.published_claim: Experimental icing and warming affect tundra plant phenology, productivity, and reproduction.
inference.scope_boundary: No causal interpretation beyond the randomized treatment design is added here.

validation.published_baseline: Full-factorial plot-level treatment comparison across years.
validation.independent_check: Preserve plot clustering and hold out a year or plot group only if the design supports it.

fragility.mechanism: Repeated measures and multiple outcomes can be mistaken for independent plot-level evidence.
fragility.alternative_explanation: Apparent treatment consistency can depend on a few plots, years, or selected outcomes.
fragility.decisive_test: Audit the plot and year hierarchy, then predeclare cluster-aware and leave-group-out checks.

decision.plain_language: The field design is useful only if plot, year, and outcome are not blended into one vague pool of evidence.
limitations: Raw files and analysis code have not been inspected.
The record does not assert that the published analysis made this error.

title: Micro- and macro-scale fatigue initiation in a hierarchical alloy

source.claim_location: Dataset abstract; README file structure and methods
source.evidence_statement: The archive describes raw and processed fatigue data, specimen IDs, analysis code, and different reported initiation mechanisms at micro and macro scales.

system.phenomenon: Scale-dependent fatigue initiation in a hierarchical alloy
system.scope_boundary: The reported microcantilever and macroscale specimen experiments.

design.time_structure: Cyclic loading from early crack initiation through extension

measurement.measurement_rule: Raw load, displacement, stiffness, crack-extension, and cycle measurements are described with processing scripts.
measurement.measurement_uncertainty: Raw values and calibration files are listed but have not been independently executed.

inference.published_claim: Different structural scales exhibit different fatigue-initiation mechanisms.
inference.scope_boundary: The cell tests whether a proposed structural analogy respects the documented scale transition.

validation.published_baseline: Scale-specific fatigue curves and documented data-processing methods.
validation.independent_check: The source documents compliance-derived crack length validated against crack-mouth opening measurements.

fragility.mechanism: Changing specimen scale changes which material structure governs fatigue initiation.
fragility.alternative_explanation: Similar curve forms can conceal different mechanisms at different scales.
fragility.decisive_test: Compare scale-specific measurements while retaining specimen identity and the calibrated measurement path.

provenance.data_location: Dryad file inventory and README, lines 35–149

decision.plain_language: A shared fatigue curve does not mean the same mechanism survives when specimen scale changes.
limitations: Only the inventory and documented processing path have been checked.
This is a counterexample to naive scaling, not a new materials claim.
